diagnoses.summary: PCA flags a large, coherent process upset dominated by reactor pressure (cstr_pressure_bar) with high SPE, suggesting a H2 PCV (vent) abnormality propagating through the process. Rule-based hints point to PCV-related faults as most likely.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset dominated by the hydrogen vent (H2 PCV) path, with a strong SPE contribution from meas.cstr_h2_vent_kmol_h. This points to a fault in the H2 PCV / venting subsystem rather than a random sensor anomaly. The most likely causes are a PCV operating fault (stuck closed or degraded capacity) causing reactor pressure rise, possibly accompanied by a secondary sensor fault.

Abnormal PCA with large coherent move and strong PCV-related contributions points to an H2 vent system fault, likely the PCV valve (stuck-closed) with possible capacity degradation; sensor bias is less likely but not ruled out.

PCA detects a large SPE-dominated upset with a coherent shift in the H2 vent and reactor pressure signals, dominated by meas.cstr_h2_vent_kmol_h. The highest rule-based evidence points to a fault in the H2 PCV path causing high reactor pressure, with the PCV either stuck or degraded, while a sensor fault on the vent measurement also contributes to the SPE.

PCA detects a large, coherent plant upset with strong CSTR pressure/vessel signals and high SPE, pointing toward a H2 PCV fault propagating through the system. The top contributing measurements are reactor pressure and H2 vent flow, with downstream loop actions trying to compensate, consistent with PCV-related issues.

The PCA anomaly is dominated by a coherent plant upset with reactor pressure rising and hydrogen vent activity driven abnormal, pointing to a faulty H2 PCV (vent valve) behavior. Likely PCV obstruction or blockage causing inadequate venting and pressure buildup.

The PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with strong H2 vent/pneumatic signature and elevated reactor temperature, dominated by a likely H2 PCV fault causing pressure build-up and compensating responses downstream.
PCA flags a strong, coherent upset with high T2 and high SPE; most likely a faulty H2 PCV actuator leading to abnormal reactor pressure dynamics.

A large, coherent plant upset with strong contribution from the CSTR pressure measurement and PCV-related signals. High T2 and high SPE indicate a process upset with strong correlation along normal directions plus a broken correlation for at least one variable, consistent with PCV (H2 vent) issues propagating through the system.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with strong contribution from CSTR pressure measurement and PCV control, with sensor fault-like behavior dominating the SPE. Likely a reactor pressure measurement bias, possibly accompanied by H2 PCV issues.

PCA flags a large coherent upset with concurrent T2 and SPE violations. Most consistent with condenser cooling loss driving high column pressure and correlated temperature disturbances, with possible H2 PCV actuator issue contributing to reactor pressure symptoms.

Abnormal PCA with large coherent shift and widespread temperature rise in distillation column trays; evidence points to condenser cooling being ineffective, with an accompanying RB_LIC loop saturation.

A large, coherent plant upset with strong SPE indicating a process-wide correlation break due to condenser cooling/PCV-driven pressure control disturbance. Saturated RB_LIC loop suggests controller authority exhausted upstream. Most likely a condenser cooling issue causing elevated tray temperatures and column pressure.

A large, coherent process upset with both T² and SPE violated; strongest evidence points to a condenser cooling effectiveness loss driving the widespread temperature rise in the distillation tray temperatures and related variables.
PCA shows a large, coherent process upset with both T2 and SPE violated. Upstream indicators point to a condenser cooling issue driving a column pressure rise and associated loop saturation (RB_LIC).

PCA flags a large, coherent upset with both T² and SPE violations, dominated by multiple tray temperature measurements and a saturated reflux control loop, consistent with a condenser cooling-related upset propagating through the column.

PCA indicates a large, coherent plant upset with significant SPE, dominated by column/condensation related variables. The most likely fault is condenser cooling loss causing reduced condenser effectiveness and abnormal column behavior; secondary hypotheses involve H2 PCV issues affecting reactor pressure.

Abnormal PCA move with large T² and SPE, with strongest evidence pointing to the H2 PCV (vent valve) as the source of the upset. The PCV-related faults best explain the observed high reactor pressure signal and the controller behavior.

High-dimensional abnormal with strong drift and drum level issues pointing to reflux/quench dynamics; sensor and PCV issues are plausible but the drum leak scenario best explains the observed drum holdup drop and saturated reflux drum loop.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with high T² and high SPE, with a saturated reflux drum loop (DR_LIC) and dominant drift from DR_LIC-related actuations and CSTR/ drum holdup measurements. Evidence points to a DR_LIC-driven disturbance, with possible secondary issues in the reflux drum and H2 PCV system contributing to the abnormal state.

PCA flags a large, coherent process upset with both T2 and SPE violated, dominated by pressure/venting related signals. Fixed-rule evidence points to an H2 PCV issue (capacity degradation or stuck closed) as the likely driver, with a possible reflux drum leak contributing to the disturbance. Several indicators suggest PCV-related upset is compensating upstream rather than a pure sensor fault.

The PCA indicates a large, coherent shift with both T2 and SPE violated, with strong contribution from the H2 PCV (vent) related signals. The evidence points to degradation or blockage of the hydrogen purge valve/vent system, causing elevated reactor pressure and compensatory controller actions.

An abnormal PCA with both T² and SPE violations, dominated by signs pointing to a hydrogen vent (H2 PCV) subsystem upset, consistent with PCV valve degradation or sticking. Likely multiple faults related to H2 PCV affecting reactor pressure control and associated transfers.

PCA flags a large shift with both T2 and SPE violations, with strongest evidence pointing to a condenser cooling effectiveness issue causing a coherent plant upset; other plausible contributors include H2 PCV issues and reboiler leaks.

Strongly abnormal PCA with large coherent movement and strong SPE, with RB_LIC loop Saturated. Evidence points to an actuator-related issue around the reboiler/heater/outlet region propagating through the CSTR/feed system, rather than a pure sensor fault.

PCA shows a large, coherent process upset with high T2 and high SPE, dominated by tray-temperature measurements and reboiler pressure/controller activity. Active loop saturation (RB_LIC) indicates the control loop is maxed out trying to compensate. The most consistent fault from the catalogue is a condenser cooling issue causing a coherent shift in multiple trays and column behavior.

PCA flags a large, coherent process upset with simultaneous T² and SPE violations. The dominant evidence points to heat-removal/cooling limitations in the condenser affecting the column, with an additional likely issue of RB_LIC being out of range (loop saturation).

PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with strong contributions from multiple tray temperatures and a saturated reboiler control loop; likely a condenser cooling effectiveness issue propagating through the column, with secondary issues in reboiler control.

PCA flags a large, coherent upset with strong SPE intrusion and high T2, dominated by tray temperature signals and a likely condenser issue. Two fixed-rule indications also point to a condenser issue and an abnormal RB_LIC actuator state. Sensor correlation disruption (SPE) suggests a process upset rather than isolated sensor fault.
A coherent plant upset with condenser cooling loss is most likely, with downstream saturation of the RB_LIC and DR_LIC loops also active.

PCA shows a large coherent upset with strong SPE, with condenser-related disturbances and several LIC loops saturated. Rule-based evidence points to condenser cooling loss as the primary fault driving the abnormal state.
High coherence-based plant upset with saturated control loops and strong contribution from high tray temperatures; evidence points to condenser cooling issue driving the disturbance.

Abnormal PCA with coherent large disturbance; multiple control loops saturated off setpoint plus strong contribution from tray temperatures. Most likely a condenser cooling efficiency loss propagating through the column, with secondary actuator/saturation faults in the reflux/outlet paths and possible H2 PCV issue.
Abnormal PCA: large coherent plant upset with both T² and SPE violations; most likely condenser cooling loss causing widespread warm-up and pressure changes in the column.

PCA detects a large, coherent process upset with simultaneous T² and SPE violations and saturated loops. Top evidence points to a condenser cooling issue driving high column temperatures and elevated pressures, with upstream loops at or near their authority limits.

PCA flags a large, coherent upset with strong SPE and T²; top contributors point to reboiler and reactor composition changes. The fixed-rule hypotheses favor a liquid leak at the reboiler as the primary fault, with condenser cooling loss and catalyst activity loss as secondary suspects.

A large, coherent process upset with multiple temperature traces affected and a high level alarm on the CSTR, consistent with a condenser cooling loss propagating through the column and reactor feed/refinement system.

PCA shows a large, coherent upset with both high Hotelling T² and high SPE, with saturated control loops and an alarm on reactor level holdup. The strongest rule-driven and feature evidence points to an upset at the CSTR outlet/feed path, most consistent with CSTR Outlet Capacity Loss, potentially accompanied by a CSTR liquid leak. Additional hints suggest condenser cooling effectiveness loss contributing to nearby tray temps and column pressure. Multiple faults may be active.

A coherent process upset with large T² and SPE, dominated by CSTR holdup and acetone-related variables, with saturated control loops and an active CSTR level alarm. Most likely a bottleneck at the CSTR outlet causing limited or lost outflow, with secondary mass-imbalance or catalyst-related effects.

PCA shows a large, coherent plant upset with both T2 and SPE violated, with strong evidence pointing to a condenser/venting related disturbance propagating through the loop controls. The rule-based hints favor condenser cooling loss and out-of-range loop outputs, consistent with a large load/utility change or a condenser/vent fault driving the upset and causing loop saturation upstream.
High coherence-dominated upset with strong contribution from multiple tray temperatures; evidence points toward loss of condenser cooling leading to abnormal column dynamics and downstream effects.

PCA shows a large, coherent process upset with concurrent SPE and T2 violations, with strongest evidence pointing to a loss of condenser cooling effectiveness affecting the distillation column; several controller outputs are saturated and running against setpoints, consistent with an upstream or condenser-side fault.

PCA indicates a large, coherent plant upset with simultaneous T² and SPE violations and multiple saturated control loops. Among fault possibilities, the evidence most strongly points to condenser cooling being ineffective, with plausible contributing issues at the H2 purge/vent (PCV) path causing elevated reactor pressure and cascading loop saturation.

PCA flags a large, coherent process upset with both T2 and SPE violations. Upstream control loops are saturated; several condenser/PCV related faults are plausible given the evidence. Most likely a condenser cooling loss causing heat buildup and pressure rise, with secondary PCV related issues contributing to reactor pressure/flow control saturation.

PCA indicates a large, coherent process upset with strong SPE, dominated by CSTR outlet-side disturbances and associated condenser/utility effects. The fixed-loop saturation and R_L_L alarm point to a CSTR liquid loss or outlet constraint, with condenser cooling becoming less effective under the upset.
